question: A gym had 85 member files. They subtracted 77 inactive members. They multiplied by 9 for a membership projection. They subtracted 16 for cancellations. Then 31 more files were removed for cleanup. Finally, 21 files were archived. Recording daily, morning, and afternoon transactions, how many active member files remain?

A farmer started with 50 apples in the morning. They added 5 more apples. Then 57 more from a second tree. They added 46 from a third tree. They subtracted 15 apples sold at market. By afternoon, 15 more apples were harvested. Finally, 19 apples were added for total count. In converting to market time, how many apples does the farmer have?

A school started with 25 students. They added 62 students in morning enrollment. They multiplied by 3 for a classroom projection. Then by 8 to account for all grades. They added 54 students. Finally, multiplied by 4 for a comprehensive enrollment count. Sarah teaches morning classes and James teaches afternoon - how many students do they jointly oversee?

A store had 59 items. They multiplied by 5 for the weekly inventory. Then by 4 for the monthly count. Then by 4 again for quarterly planning. They added 68 items from restocking. Between morning and evening inventory checks, Michael and Lisa counted items - how many total items are there?

A project had 151 tasks. They subtracted 61 completed tasks. Then added 7 newly identified tasks. They added 54 more tasks. They multiplied by 4 for a tracking system. They subtracted 499 cancelled tasks. Finally, 37 tasks were recovered. In terms of team workload and milestones, how many tasks remain?

A bakery had 50 batches. They multiplied by 3 for morning production. Then by 7 for daily total. They added 15 more batches. They multiplied by 4 for a week's projection. Finally, 1891 batches from a large contract were subtracted. Using 'a dozen' as a measure, how many batches does the bakery track?

A logistics hub had 238 packages. They multiplied by 9 for initial sorting. Then by 3 for regional distribution. Then by 3 for sub-regional sorting. Then by 5 for final delivery routes. Finally, 14 packages were added as amendments. Morning, afternoon, and evening deliveries were made by Marcus and Jennifer - what is the total package count?

A sports team had 90 balls. They multiplied by 5 during supply ordering. Then by 8 for the full season inventory. They added 32 balls from donations. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for competition planning. In the morning, Sarah organized equipment; in the afternoon, Marcus counted supplies - how many balls are in their final inventory?

A farm had 26 acres. They doubled the planted area. They added 78 acres from new purchases. They divided by 2 for crop rotation. They subtracted 35 acres for conservation. They added 20 more for expansion. Finally, they multiplied by 4 for a land management plan. One neighboring property had 50 acres but was not included. What is the final acreage?

A company had 163 projects. They multiplied by 7 for a portfolio review. They subtracted 847 completed initiatives. They divided by 3 for team allocation. They subtracted 23 cancelled projects. They multiplied by 4 for tracking purposes. Then divided by 4 for a final accounting. From morning through evening, how many active projects are there?

A store started with 111 items. They subtracted 35 items sold. They multiplied by 4 for a shelf planning layout. They subtracted 125 damaged items. They multiplied by 6 for storage capacity calculation. Finally, 64 items were added during restocking. Using minutes and hours as a unit conversion, what is the final count?

A warehouse had 210 packages. They multiplied by 4 during receiving. Then by 2 for inventory sorting. They added 79 packages from new shipments. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for distribution planning. Between Rachel (day shift manager) and Tom (night shift manager), how many packages are accounted for?

A bakery had 225 loaves. They multiplied by 4 for the full-day production. They added 9 loaves from a special order. They doubled the total for next-day planning. They subtracted 50 loaves for retail fulfillment. The bakery uses minutes and hours for scheduling - what is the projected loaf count?

A manager had 171 files to process. They subtracted 55 completed files. Then 73 more files were finished. They subtracted 9 files for archive. Then 1 file was removed by mistake. Finally, 24 files were sent for shredding. Using hours and minutes as time conversion, how many files remain active?

A storage facility had 186 boxes. They subtracted 68 boxes removed for an event. They divided by 2 to organize two sections. They subtracted 37 more boxes used. They subtracted 13 damaged boxes. Finally, they multiplied by 8 for capacity planning. One warehouse location had separate storage but wasn't counted here. How many boxes are in the final plan?

A manufacturer had 102 units. They multiplied by 5 for production. Then by 3 for doubled shifts. Then by 3 for team assignments. Then by 6 for facility capability. Finally, they multiplied by 3 for expansion planning. They subtracted 12138 units from a major order. Between James (production lead) and Alice (planning), how many units remain?

A warehouse started with 103 items. They added 64 items from a delivery. They multiplied by 6 for a weekly count. Then by 5 for monthly planning. They subtracted 2908 items from a major fulfillment. Finally, 999 items were deducted for returns. Between Rita (inventory) and Leon (warehouse), how many items remain?

A library had 134 books. They subtracted 24 books for repairs. They divided by 2 for two-location split. They added 53 books from a donation. Then 17 more books arrived. Finally, 68 books were added from a book drive. Using minutes instead of books, what is the final count?

A store had 208 items. They added 66 items from restocking. They subtracted 125 items sold. They added 39 more items. Finally, 45 items were added. Using a time-ordered approach from morning through evening, what is the final inventory?

A school had 31 desks initially. They subtracted 27 desks sent to repair. They added 44 new desks. They subtracted 29 desks for another classroom. They multiplied by 4 for a comprehensive classroom setup. Finally, 34 desks were added. Using the word 'double', how many desks are in Maria and David's classrooms combined?

A library had 162 books. They subtracted 128 books checked out. They subtracted 8 more books sent for binding. They doubled the remainder. They subtracted 1 book removed by error. They subtracted 25 books for archiving. Finally, 18 books were removed. Between Margaret (morning) and Robert (evening), using the word 'double', how many books remain?

A farm had 232 carrots. They added 53 carrots from a second harvest. They multiplied by 4 for a restaurant order. They divided by 5 to allocate to five locations. Finally, 18 more carrots were added. Using a morning-to-evening production timeline, how many carrots are in the final allocation?

A warehouse had 124 items. They added 76 items from a shipment. Then 79 more arrived. They subtracted 261 items fulfilled for orders. They multiplied by 6 to plan inventory. Finally, they divided by 2 for dual-location tracking. Between morning and evening, how many items are managed?

A storage facility started with 231 boxes. They subtracted 36 boxes removed. They multiplied by 6 for capacity calculation. Then by 9 for a comprehensive assessment. They added 13 boxes from new stock. Finally, 4441 boxes were withdrawn for distribution. In terms of inventory changes through the day, how many boxes remain?

A farm started with 220 liters. They divided by 5 to allocate to sections. They subtracted 43 liters used. They added 76 liters from new collection. Finally, 26 liters were removed for processing. Using the word 'half', from morning preparation through evening calculations, how many liters remain?
